subject.title: [Feature]: Support custom HTTP headers on CLI WebSocket connections

question: Should OpenClaw add custom Gateway CLI WebSocket headers, and which credential-safe input sources and precedence should become the supported public contract?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but arbitrary headers can carry reverse-proxy credentials and change the Gateway connection/auth boundary, so automation should not choose the permanent CLI/env/config contract.

options.title: Approve a narrow secret-safe contract
options.body: Add header forwarding through maintainer-approved sources only, with SecretInput/env substitution, redaction, docs, and tests for fresh and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Limit support to explicit CLI headers
options.body: Support only repeatable per-invocation headers for now, avoiding durable config/env persistence at the cost of CI and automation ergonomics.

options.title: Decline core header support
options.body: Keep SSH, Tailscale, and local proxy workflows as the supported paths and document reverse-proxy header injection as outside OpenClaw CLI.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow secret-safe contract
recommendation.body: Add header forwarding through maintainer-approved sources only, with SecretInput/env substitution, redaction, docs, and tests for fresh and upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest combined history on Gateway WebSocket design, remote Gateway config, and the sibling mobile credential-header decision.
